title: Soft-signal memo: engineering fit — Nyla Ibrahim
body:
Late-night brain dump after loop with Nyla — want to capture the soft signals while they're fresh. This is less about checklist scores and more about the behavioral/heuristic impressions that matter for senior runtime hires. Intention: raw input for panel calibration and an optional short trial design if we lean toward a hire.

Quick TL;DR:
- Strong systems intuition, especially around cache/consistency tradeoffs.
- Comfortable with messy constraints (partial KV cache, multi-tenant eviction) — gave practical, bounded solutions instead of idealized designs.
- Communication: tends toward pragmatic clarity but occasionally glosses over edge cases when under time pressure.
- Risk: limited exposure to our exact infra (thin experience with Triton-like serving), but heavy on distributed systems patterns; likely rampable.

Notes (verbatim-style):
- Started with warm-up Q on LRU vs. segmented LRU for KV caches. Nyla sketched segmented LRU + per-tenant admission gates. Mentioned tradeoffs with tail latency and eviction churn — liked that she brought up admission control as a knob for p99.
- When asked about cold-starts and model paging, proposed a two-tier cache: fast on-GPU KV for hot prefixes + compressed off-GPU store that can hydrate asynchronously. Emphasized correctness over speculative micro-optimizations.
- On autoscaling: suggested demand signals combining request queue depth and average token completion times; recommended short, conservative scaleouts with a fast fallback lane (lower-capacity cheaper instances) for bursty tails. Pragmatic.
- Observability thinking: wants tracing per-request with token-level spans to attribute costs. Not novel but realistic; has an instinct for debuggability.
- Coding pair: did a short pairing step implementing a simplified admission gate in pseudocode. Mostly solid; some minor style nitpicks (local variable naming), but algorithmic approach was clear. Missed one off-by-one in ring-buffer index during review — called out and fixed quickly. Shows iterate-and-correct.

Behavioral signals:
- Collaborative: asked follow-ups, validated constraints from interviewer before proposing wide designs.
- Time-pressure: when pressed, tended to jump to a favored pattern (cache + admission) and glossed the queuing consequences until prompted. Not a blocker, but worth watching in fast-decision environments.
- Product sense: repeatedly brought up developer ergonomics (debuggable metrics, simple default configs). That maps well to our dev-first emphasis.

Red flags / Unknowns:
- Limited direct experience with model-runtime-specific kernels (XLA, custom CUDA kernels). Has read and toyed but hasn't shipped kernel-level perf wins.
- Has not run a multi-tenant production serving fleet at 50k qps. Has experience at tens of k qps on autoscaling backend stacks, but need to validate ops experience.
- Interview didn't dig deeply into security/multi-tenant isolation mechanisms (namespaces, cgroups, SGX/KMS workflows). Might need an ops-focused follow-up.

Suggested probing / follow-up tasks if we want more evidence:
1) Small take-home: design + rough cost/latency analysis for a prefix caching layer that supports pinned-user prefixes (500MB hot working set) and can fall back to a compressed store. Ask for cost breakdown and quick pseudocode for admission logic. 48-72 hour turnaround.
2) Ops deep-dive: 45 min async call with SRE lead to go over incident postmortems (ask candidate to walk through one relevant incident they owned and the specific mitigations).
3) Pairing: 90-minute pair on a tight latency bug (simulate KV eviction noise causing p99 spikes) — measure how they debug and instrument.

Suggested score snapshot (rough heuristics, 1-5):
- System design (serving/runtime): 4
- Low-level performance knowledge (kernels/CUDA): 2.5
- Debugging & observability: 4
- Communication & cross-team: 4
- Ops/production ownership: 3
Overall gut: 3.5/5 — leaning positive if we can validate ops/infra exposure.

Hiring recommendation options (for calibration doc):
- Strong "fit for staff engineer" if trial confirms ops background; otherwise consider as senior engineer with focused ramp plan.
- If we pass, highlight mentorship on kernel-level perf and runbook ownership in first 3 months.

Action items from me (Ravi):
- Share take-home sketch + scoring rubric to Ari (hiring partner) and Avery for quick review.
- Post quick note to #hiring-runtime with 2-line synopsis and request SRE pairing availability.
- If we greenlight trial, draft a short 3-week ramp plan focused on (1) observability project, (2) incident playbook, (3) a small perf microbenchmark.

Open questions I still have:
- Does Nyla have resume examples of incidents where she owned both the incident and follow-up systemic fix? (I remember a sentence about "led platform incident" but want details.)
- What are exact endpoints she has run in prod (qps, model sizes)?
- Comfort level with CUDA / kernel-level debugging — willing to invest in training?

Notes-to-self: keep feedback crisp and avoid over-indexing on CUDA skill gap if ops/product instincts are strong. Our runtime hires often learn kernel specifics on the job if they have strong systems intuition and shipping experience.

End of dump. Use freely for panel calibration. Will refine into a 1-paragraph summary for the panel vote doc tomorrow.
